cards.text: Friend, we're with John, the servant who was shown this whole vision (Revelation 1:1). He just watched earth and heaven flee from the presence of the One on a great white throne (Revelation 20:11). Now John looks again, and the first heaven and earth have passed away.

cards.question: The first heaven and earth have passed away. What does John see now?

answers.text: A new heaven and a new earth
A wide desert under a dark sky
An empty sky over deep waters

cards.text: And John notices one more thing: the sea is no more.
Then John sees the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God. Baker, I get nervous lifting a cookie box off the top shelf, and here comes a whole CITY.

cards.question: You know I'm baking for a wedding feast, friend. So how is the new Jerusalem prepared as it comes down out of heaven?

answers.text: As a bride adorned for her husband
As a crown set with every jewel
As a king's house ready for guests

cards.question: Then a loud voice from the throne speaks. It says the dwelling place of God is with man.

cards.text: The voice also says they will be His people, and God Himself will be with them as their God. He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.

cards.question: The voice from the throne says there will be no more death or crying, because the ___ things have passed away.
Now the One seated on the throne speaks. He says He makes all things ___.
The One on the throne tells John, "Write this down…" Why does He say to?

answers.text: These words are faithful and true
John might forget what he saw
The angels want a record of it

cards.text: Then the One on the throne says, "It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End."

cards.question: The One on the throne speaks of the spring of the water of life. Who does He say He will give it to freely?

cards.text: Then the One on the throne makes a promise to the one who overcomes: "…I will be his God, and he will be My son."

cards.question: The One on the throne says the one who overcomes will inherit only a small share.

cards.text: But then He speaks of the lake that burns with fire and sulfur. He says, "This is the second death."

cards.question: The One on the throne just promised the overcomer everything. Whose place does He say will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur?

answers.text: The cowardly and unbelieving and all liars
Everyone who lived on the first earth
Anyone who never saw the new city

cards.text: Then one of the seven angels with the seven bowls of the seven final plagues says to John, "Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb." The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29), and His Supper is the one I'm baking for (Revelation 19:9), so baker, I am LEANING in.
The angel carries John away in the Spirit to a mountain great and high. There he shows John the holy city of Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God.

cards.question: The holy city of Jerusalem is shining as it comes down. What is it shining with?

cards.text: Its radiance is like a most precious jewel, like a jasper, as clear as crystal. The shiniest thing in my bakery is a freshly scrubbed cookie sheet, and next to this city it's a mud puddle.
The city has a great, high wall with twelve gates, three on each side. And there are twelve angels at the gates.

cards.question: The twelve gates of the city bear the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.
The city wall has twelve foundations, and they bear names too: the twelve ___ of the Lamb.

cards.text: Then the angel measures the city with a golden rod: 12,000 stadia long, wide AND high, all equal. The city is pure gold, the wall is jasper, the foundations are adorned with every kind of precious stone, and each of the twelve gates is one single pearl. ONE pearl per gate, baker, and I got picked up at a bakery's closing sale for a quarter.

cards.question: John sees no temple anywhere in the new Jerusalem. Why not?

answers.text: The Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple
The people worship outside its walls
The old temple stayed behind on the old earth

cards.question: The city has no need of sun or moon. The glory of God gives it light, and the Lamb is its ___.
The kings of the earth will bring their glory into the city. And who will walk by the city's light?
The gates of the new Jerusalem are shut at the end of each day.
The glory and honor of the nations will be brought into the city, but nothing unclean will ever enter it. Who does enter?

answers.text: Those whose names are written in the Lamb's Book of Life
Those who carry gold and jewels up to its gates
Those who were born and raised inside its walls

cards.text: The angel isn't done showing John around. Next he shows him a river of the water of life, as clear as crystal.

cards.question: The river of the water of life flows from the ___ of God and of the Lamb.

cards.text: The river runs down the middle of the city's main street. And that street is pure gold, as clear as glass.

cards.question: On either side of the river stands a tree of ___.

cards.text: Same name as the tree in the garden of Eden (Genesis 2:9), and it bears TWELVE kinds of fruit. I've got six toppings and I still stand there every morning like it's the hardest decision of my life.

cards.question: The tree of life by the river bears its fruit only once a year.

cards.text: Even the leaves have a job. They're for the healing of the nations.

cards.question: In the new Jerusalem, John says one thing will no longer be there at all. What is it?

cards.text: The throne of God and of the Lamb will be right there in the city. And His servants will worship Him.

cards.question: In the city, God's servants will see His face.

cards.text: His name will be on their foreheads. And no night, no lamp, no sun needed, because the Lord God will shine on them.

cards.question: The Lord God shines on His servants in the city. How long will they reign?
